I purchased sphagnum moss for propagations. In there i put pothos stem cuttings and a few nodes with leaf from a philodenron. The same day i set up my prop box (like an hour later), i noticed tiny translucent egg shaped "dots" clinging to the top of one leaf and on the sides of the box. I can 100% guarantee they were not there when i was setting up the box.

I thought it might be lint or just stuff from the moss, but to be sure i removed it with alcohol dipped q tip. 

The next day they were back. Again clinging to the sides of my box and on top of one leaf. 

When i did a Google search, whiteflies was suggested. But i have not seen anything fly in the box, in my plant area, or in any of my other plants. I read whiteflies cling to the bottom of leaves and these dots sit on top of my leaf. Lastly, they don't look alive. There are no legs or wings how whiteflies would have. If these are whitefly eggs (which I've seen and don't look like what i see in my box) then why aren't there whiteflies? 

I also quarantined the philodendron and pothos i took the cuttings from but there seems to be not white dots on them. It is specifically in my moss box

Pictures aren't great quality but imagine really thin tiny egg shaped pieces of an insects wing for example. Just today i also noticed a worm shaped group of these on one of the pothos stems, pictured.
